question: Does added historical evidence identify the route actually taken beyond finding a route that successfully reproduces the artifact?
scope: Native finite supplied-law ruler with exact executable routes, paired historical prefixes and a direct enumeration reference. Learned reconstruction, unknown libraries and human process correspondence remain conditional.
world: Four equally likely persistent makers. Each world draws a 2 by 4 by 4 table of method probabilities from a Dirichlet distribution with concentration 5 for the maker-preferred method and 1 otherwise. For goal zero preference is maker index; for goal one it is the next method cyclically. Goals are independent fair bits. Four methods produce either binary goal exactly: set goal; set opposite then flip; set goal then flip twice; set opposite, inspect, then flip. Their lengths are 1, 2, 3, 3.
observations: Current goal equals the visible artifact. Past complete goal/method records share the same maker. Current witness is absent, inspection presence, or complete method. Every history length takes a prefix of the same 64-event stream; current and future outcomes stay paired. Future choice is method under the opposite supplied goal, not the already determined endpoint.

readers.shortest: Shortest method consistent with artifact and current witness, deterministic. Future maker belief conditions on current witness only; past history is deliberately unused.
readers.goal-plausible: Modal method under population law conditional on goal and current witness. Future belief matches the no-history historical reader; past history is unused.
readers.historical: Supplied-law posterior integrates persistent makers using past records and current witness; gives distributions over actual current method and future method.
readers.direct-enumeration: Independent scalar sum over the same four maker states and all route outcomes with identical evidence. Exact distribution matching is an information/implementation control, not a fitted architecture comparison.

scores: uncapped current-route log loss with explicit infinite fractions
controls: all eight programs reach their declared endpoint
distinct histories share exactly the same endpoint
uniform maker policies make past records uninformative
a complete current witness identifies the route
every scalar posterior agrees with the independent enumeration
complete engineering consumers and bounded full-grid pilot
complete frozen-source scientific replay before acceptance
fixtures: Twelve blind route-ambiguity/inspection cases exercise the canonical ProcessCase validator and offline exporter read-only, with executable candidate routes public and actual route/posterior evaluator-only. These extend existing alias/inspection semantics; they do not claim omission, decisive selection or retraction coverage.
analysis: Pair all cases, readers, history lengths and witness conditions within each coefficient world. Bootstrap world-level contrasts with 4096 draws. Separate successful reenactment, historical accuracy, future prediction, observation privilege and computation. No original-world B/C superiority gate is inherited.
continuation: Land the exact route/history distinction and its fixtures after full replay. Prioritize registered C05 omission, E01 decisive-selection and D05 retraction consumers; retain learned reconstruction and candidate-specific controls as conditional scope. Stop claims that reenactment alone identifies the actual historical route.
limitations: Maker policy and complete route catalog are supplied. Ignoring history in heuristic readers is an evidence restriction, not a fair learned capacity test. Current witnesses add information; exact direct enumeration matches the historical posterior. Miniature — architecture untested. No fresh confirmation or live downstream reader inference.
